prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: full-fidelity desktop portfolio landing-page direction comp, 1536 by 1024 landscape
Primary request: Design an actual responsive website viewport for COLTON SPURGIN using an architectural daylight-section composition. The visitor must understand who Colton is, what he has done, and whether his working style fits them.
Scene/backdrop: no scene; this is a flat front-facing website screenshot
Subject: a candid personal portfolio for an Air Force NCO, lead software developer intern, research assistant, and UWF senior specializing in AI who graduates December 2026 and wants to build useful ambitious software before pursuing a master’s degree
Style/medium: high-fidelity editorial web UI inspired by architectural section drawings, limewash paper, measured ink, and daylight-analysis annotation
Composition/framing: thin top navigation with COLTON SPURGIN at left and WORK, EXPERIENCE, ABOUT, CONTACT at right; below it, one wide continuous architectural cutaway occupies most of the fold, moving left to right through four distinct rooms labeled AIR FORCE NCO, LEAD SOFTWARE DEVELOPER INTERN, RESEARCH ASSISTANT, and AI SPECIALIZATION · UWF · DEC 2026; a strong but quiet headline sits to the left, “I BUILD SYSTEMS, LEARN HARD PROBLEMS, AND CARE ABOUT DOING USEFUL WORK WELL.”; below the section drawing, show the start of a selected-work band with BORK, VELLM, TSP BENCHMARKS, and HOME LAB as real project labels. Make one amber daylight beam the dominant visual move. Keep all other regions restrained.
Color palette: limewash #f2efea, charcoal #1c1f22, sunbeam #d6a43a, shadow blue #5b6b7c
Materials/textures: subtle uncoated paper grain, architectural ink lines, sparse measured annotations
Text (verbatim): “COLTON SPURGIN”; “WORK”; “EXPERIENCE”; “ABOUT”; “CONTACT”; “I BUILD SYSTEMS, LEARN HARD PROBLEMS, AND CARE ABOUT DOING USEFUL WORK WELL.”; “AIR FORCE NCO”; “LEAD SOFTWARE DEVELOPER INTERN”; “RESEARCH ASSISTANT”; “AI SPECIALIZATION · UWF · DEC 2026”; “SELECTED WORK”; “BORK”; “VELLM”; “TSP BENCHMARKS”; “HOME LAB”; “VIEW THE WORK”
Constraints: this must read unmistakably as a usable desktop website, not a poster or an architecture project; all core UI copy must be legible; factual and restrained; no portrait photo; no logo; no invented employers, metrics, awards, testimonials, or project claims
Avoid: generic SaaS cards, bento grid, neon cyber aesthetic, 3D mockup, browser chrome, decorative laptop or phone, illegible pseudo-text, gradients, rounded pill buttons, heavy shadows, watermark
